First session of the Post Quantum transaction signature (PQTS) Breakout Room

# Agenda overview

This inaugural call focuses on high-level overviews, expectation setting, and community alignment for the Post Quantum transaction signature (PQTS).

**Agenda**:

* Introduction to PQTS and its goals
* Walk-through of the [current](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8051) [EIPs](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8052) 
* [New AA](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8141) and long term vision
* [Zero-Knowledge proof of seed as a graceful emergency fallback](https://ethresear.ch/t/how-to-hard-fork-to-save-most-users-funds-in-a-quantum-emergency/18901)  
* [Cryptographic Agility](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1889#issuecomment-3786344321)

comments.body: Is this just for the algos for PQ or are surrounding EIPs also discussed? ie https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11144
@chunter-cb mainly algos for PQ but interaction with AA is definitely in scope

Some things I think we need to consider:

* Cryptographic Agility (the ability to add/remove algos without major protocol changes)
* Hardware wallet feasibility for the algorithms
* The importance of aligning with signatures from spec bodies like NIST, ISO, ITU-T, IETF (is it important or not important?)

I'd like to join this call but I am unfortunately busy so I'll tldr what I would've contributed here:

- **Cryptographic Agility**: Being able to swap out signature algorithms without breaking all existing infrastucture is as important as migrating to PQ algorithms in the first place.
- **EIP Interactions**: With protocol level signatures the main candidates (at least in my opinion) are [EIP-6404](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6404) or [EIP-7701](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7701). EIP-6404 because of the EIP-7932 integration and EIP-7701 because it can push verification logic to the EVM. I think it would be reasonable to expect another proposal for RLP transactions that verify with the EIP-7932 interface.

  It also appears that while EIPs [8051](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8051) and [8052](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8052), define EIP-7932 integration in addition to the precompiles, it cannot be implemented in their current form as it uses the outdated interface and uses undefined functions (`lookup_pubkey`).
- **Public keys**: There needs to be some way to handle/store public keys, whether that storing it in an EOAs storage, systems contract, account trie, etc.

* EIP-6404 - SSZ is going to make things harder, that discussion has been had many times on ACDE resisting SSZ on the EL and there are many devs holding firm on not adopting it. Using CA transactions as leverage will not make things easier. We should consider an RLP alternative.

* Public Keys - The problem with storing pubkeys on the ledgers is that the transactions themselves are not self-certifying. You would need another lookup table based on a presumed "from address" to the pubkey. An obvious design choice is to ship the pubkey with the signature.  ECDSA having extratable signatures was incredibly useful, but it is far from a universal feature of most DSA algos, not just PQ ones either.

> We should consider an RLP alternative.

@shemnon This is what I had in mind, I wanted to wait until things stabilized before pushing for a new proposal. Especially with the complexity of migrating the entire network to PQ algorithms. I'd guess we have at least a couple more network upgrades until quantum threats start to emerge so initially pushing for the pure AA method, e.g. 7932, ERC-4337 should make later implementation of PQ for EOA transactions less complex later down the line.

Assuming there are no new transaction formats needed between now and then.  IMHO any new TX format from here on out needs to support CA, wether that is in a unified new tx format or if the signatures are somehow portable. Even if it's just ECDSA that is supported by mainnet.

I do think we need to get started on standard ALG_TYPE registries as Tempo has a similar algo mapping in their tx. I know the EIP editors hate list EIPs but...

Also, 8 bits may not be enough for a 100 year registry. You might wake up one morning and discover SLH-DSA has 12 more parameter sets that need to be supported across 3 hash types and that's just on Tuesday.  So maybe RLP(ALG_TYPE) so while n is small it acts like 7-bit ascii?

> Also, 8 bits may not be enough for a 100 year registry

I partially disagree here, while 8 bits may not be enough for 100 years, it is definitely good enough until the whole PQ spaces settles (given that [NIST is only up to 46 algorithms](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/computer-security-objects-register/algorithm-registration#SLH-DSA) for RSA, ECC, ML-DSA and all variants of SLH-DSA). If we do run out of algorithm entries we could always set a specific `ALG_TYPE` as an extension varint type i.e. `0xFD || uleb128_alg_type_that_is_greater_than_256 || signature`.

Hi everyone, 
I am Jayamine Alupotha, a cryptography researcher with a keen interest in the next chapter of post-quantum secure Ethereum. In this meeting, I am looking forward to seeing the decisions made to enhance cryptographic agility. I believe that improving cryptographic agility is crucial not only for making Ethereum resistant to quantum attacks but also for adapting to new techniques that may emerge, especially if they prove to be faster than the existing ones. 
 Looking forward to the meeting.
You can find a detailed exposition the ideas we just presented here: https://github.com/neverlocal/eth-graceful-emergency-fallback/blob/main/whitepaper.pdf
